versions.quote: This lack of daily maintenance can show up in many ways. As our lives become more comfortable, many of us lapse into spiritual complacency, and we find ourselves in the same horror and loss of purpose from which we came. We forget we are given only a daily reprieve. We must ask for help each morning and remember to thank God at night. If we do not maintain our spiritual condition daily, some of us find the resulting pain and confusion lead to a return to drugs and our old way of life. Some have made it back from relapses ... many have not." Gray Book
versions.body:
When we came to NA our daily maintenance consisted of one thing....the getting and using and finding ways and means to use. We went to any lengths to get drugs yet expect recovery to happen by osmosis. There are days when we may wake up, rushing and forgetting to thank our Higher Power for another day clean. The days we don’t start our day with prayer and meditation, a lack of gratitude can sink in. We allow ourselves to fall into complacency, when we forget to be grateful and rob ourselves from staying in the moment. This complacency pulls us further away from our recovery and from the basics that got us and kept us clean in the beginning. Complacency is dangerous for an addict. Skipping Step work, prayer, meditation, meetings and not reaching out to another recovering addict are signs of a lack of daily maintenance. We no longer participate in any Group or individual service. Many have said they were baffled at how they lost their way, while others have been heard to say they simply stopped their daily maintenance. Some of us have heard a common theme and that was a loss of connection.... with the "fellowship, with their Higher Power, with others in general." It seems the return to isolation as in our past was a common factor for many. So due to lack of daily spiritual maintenance when life on life's terms becomes overwhelming and we're feeling burnt out through personal responsibilities, we can create a sense of alienation towards meetings because we stop doing what we're doing. We pull further into isolation. Prayer and meditation feel meaningless and trying to stay connected with other addicts becomes difficult. Through daily maintenance when things do feel hard, renewing our commitment to recovery won't be as challenging. Long clean time can be an extremely dangerous place for addicts as it can lead to complacency. This is why we see so many come and go from the rooms. Some of us have heard the first year is free. Now it is time to put in the work. Just like everything in life we must learn consistency to grow. Some of our long timers have been heard

to say when asked: How did you do it? What is the secret? The reply: "Stick to the Basics". Keeping it simple is a gift that some forget. What we hopefully learned in our early days, works as well now as it did in the past. They say a grateful addict never uses. When we lose our gratitude, we forget the hard work it took to get to a point of freedom. By waking up and beginning our day in prayer and meditation, we acknowledge our Higher Power and all the beauty in our lives. We learn how to practice the principles in all our affairs by utilizing the 5 tools: we call addicts, pray, read NA literature, write Steps and attend meetings. These tools have never failed when implemented daily.
versions.moment: We can’t stay clean on yesterday's shower just like we can’t stay clean on yesterday's recovery. It is essential for us to stay in the basics and to put forth the effort to stay clean on a daily basis, despite what’s happening in our lives.

versions.quote: 10 things to be Grateful for after some time. "Alienation and isolation are symptoms of the mental part of our disease. To the practicing addict, life is just a movement between connections and oblivion.
versions.body:
When we used drugs, we felt like we finally found the answer because we felt connected and capable of being ourselves, or so we thought. When we didn’t have drugs, we felt depleted and inadequate. It’s no wonder we became addicted. We needed drugs to feel like normal people, and that worked…until it didn’t. Eventually, in desperation we found ourselves in Narcotics Anonymous. During active addiction, alienation and isolation was a defense mechanism to survive. At first, we didn't want people around that would disapprove of the lifestyle we had chosen for ourselves. Then, we simply didn't want people around that would use our drugs. We were selfish and self-centered. As addicts, we want more than anything to make connections in our lives but connecting feels so dangerous. We know we surround ourselves with sick people that are just as self-centered as we are. We know they would throw us to the wolves for another fix because we would do the same thing to them. So, our bonds were shallow, and—for our own protection—they remained that way. This lack of deep connection made us feel not only alone—but abandoned—until we came to the rooms of Narcotics Anonymous. We felt disconnected with the people with which we used drugs because they didn't seem to have the same values as us. We were burned and broken, and when the money was gone, so were our friends. Some still feel disconnected because we haven't learned how to express our thoughts and emotions properly. Now, playing catch up, we don't feel equal to our peers. We separate ourselves from everyone else instead of letting others into our lives. Loved ones didn't understand. We blamed everyone but ourselves for the insanity we created. We kind of hated people. We don't know why, but we don't try to figure it out. We just roll with it because we have to. We don't try, we just do. We used to only do drugs. Now, it seems like we only try to connect with people. We have a really hard time with that. Sometimes we wake up and feel immediately disconnected. We're needy and when we can't feel good right now—sound familiar?—we feel rage in our hearts and minds. We're very sick. Denial ran rampant as we struggled to let go of resentments, anger, fear, etc. Living in the moment seemed impossible. How can we live in moments we aren't even in? Oblivion became the norm and using consumed every part of our lives. How do we get out of this sickness—this disease? NA provided a way for us out of the insanity. NA suggests to cleanse our bodies of all mood-changing and mind-altering drugs if we wanted to recover. This was necessary to face those feelings and fears we had been running from for so long. We keep trying to connect...no matter what. Even when we feel that it's not working, we keep trying. Not feeling connected is almost as bad as doing drugs, if that makes sense. And

we don't do drugs anymore. So we just try to connect. We connect to recover. We connect to heal. When we arrived, we found the connections we so longed for. For the first time, we were loved because we were addicts, not in spite of it. We could be broken and still be loved. We had found a group of people that just wanted to see us thrive and find peace of mind. Calling other addicts regularly is one of our strongest tools that we have to fight isolation. Never Alone, Never Again, is about being in action. We ask for numbers from other addicts and call them daily. We begin to find hope instead of choosing to be alone. When life's issues arise, we now have a support system ready to share their Experience, Strength, and Hope. We can identify with others, and now—with God, the 12-Steps, the 12 Traditions, our Sponsor, and the Fellowship—we do recover.
versions.moment: We are given the gift of finding out we are Never Alone, Never Again. Now, as part of the NA Fellowship, we feel safe and accepted for the first time. We, then are able to join the human race as well. WE BELONG.

versions.quote: Jail did not help us at all. Medicine, religion and psychiatry seemed to have no answers for us that we could use. All these methods having failed for us, in desperation, we sought help from each other in Narcotics Anonymous.
versions.source: Gray Book pg 23 italicized header "Why are we here"
versions.body: We went to jail, still used. We went to the psychiatrist, still used. We tried by ourselves over and over, still used. There literally were no other methods that had worked for us in the past. Before we finally got clean in Narcotics Anonymous, there were many forms of institutions and programs that society thought could help us: time outs, detention during the schooldays, juvenile centers, psych wards, prisons, detox, drug rehabilitation centers, drug programs, emergency wards and when we exhausted any and all those sources we were on people’s couches. We begged people for a short-term solution but ultimately, WE knew we didn’t want to stop completely. When NA's subcommittees of (Hospitals and Institutions and Public Information) brought the NA message to those institutions, we thought they were giving the help to others and not us. Using drugs was just a means to an end; essentially, our disease was the addictive process to self-obsession. Before we could find recovery and begin to fill the hole in our souls, first we had to completely abstain from all mind altering and mood changing chemicals. Everything, every place and every method we ever tried prior to NA failed. Let's face it when we got here almost everyone, we came into contact with tried curing us. Most of us were preached at, preached over, prescribed drugs to change us, some had been in jail or prison. The thing all of us had in common was that our lives were not improving despite all that offered help. Every one of the methods we attempted, claimed to have either a "Cure" or some way they thought we could stop using, including forcing us to, temporarily. None of them really got through in any kind of lasting manner and our using continued to progress. Most did not view our problem as a "disease" we were labeled in all sorts of different ways. Morally corrupt, mentally deranged etc, etc. When we are obsessing over something, calling another addict can pull us out of the loop. This time, we are reaching out for help because we cannot do it by ourselves and need a process and community - no matter how much we want to isolate. What works for those that choose the NA way is to have a Fellowship of addicts that understand the disease of addiction and are living the Steps to help us. No one understands an addict like an addict. That is why it is easy for us to call each other out on our BS. We can spot BS because we all earned our BS degree from the school of hard knocks. The NA fellowship is only part of the total solution. NA is a spiritual program that requires reaching a state of desperation, so we find the Gift Of Desperation that is necessary for this program to work. No one can do it for us. Enforced morality lacks power and it must be our choice to change if we are going to. When we are ready, we take the Steps and learn they are the way for us to start to climb out of the pit of insanity we had dug for ourselves.
versions.moment: Once we found Narcotics Anonymous most of us realized we had found others who were & are just like us. Finding others who had suffered like us was such a relief

versions.quote: Grey Book Reflections 10-08-2019 “When we refuse to practice acceptance we are, in effect, denying our faith in a Higher Power. This can lead to many problems and failures.
versions.body: Just for Today We have been sitting in our own creative misery, most likely blaming others for our problems. We in our own minds have to come to terms that we are addicts and that will never change, our addiction will just get easier to handle in our everyday lives. Being accepted to being and addict within our own self is a very big step in order to keep faith and understanding of our higher power. versions.body: Once coming to the Fellowship of NA it took some of us a while to come to realize we were in the grips of the addiction process. As our thinking cleared, we were able to see the many areas of our lives are impacted; through prayer and action we began the process of recovery. No one can admit our defeat but us. We have to do it. Even when results of our disease are visible, we still can find ourselves in denial. We had to reach our bottom and put the shovel down. As we surrender to reality, we get more honest with ourselves. This is the point where recovery can start. We felt if we laid down the drugs it would fix the problem, we did not realize we had a spiritual disease. Recovery requires we address all areas of our addictive personalities: Physical, Mental and Emotional. In order to fully recover, we had to adhere to complete and total surrender. Since we are impatient people who always wanted results not making efforts to get it - recovery requires being patient. ". This is the moment where our sponsors point out that we cannot recover overnight and we should make some efforts and place results of them in God's hands. Many of us have thought "Why I do I feel this way" or "I should be further in this road". Having surrendered our addiction to our Higher Power we began to take inventory and change our lives. This can be done only with practicing spiritual principles of the program on daily basis.

versions.body: Once coming to the Fellowship of NA it took some of us a while to come to realize we were in the grips of the addiction process. As our thinking cleared, we were able to see the many areas of our lives are impacted; through prayer and action we began the process of recovery. No one can admit our defeat but us. We have to do it. Even when results of our disease are visible, we still can find ourselves in denial. We had to reach our bottom and put the shovel down. As we surrender to reality, we get more honest with ourselves. This is the point where recovery can start. We felt if we laid down the drugs it would fix the problem, we did not realize we had a spiritual disease. Recovery requires we address all areas of our addictive personalities: Physical, Mental and Emotional. In order to fully recover, we had to adhere to complete and total surrender. Since we are impatient people who always wanted results not making efforts to get it - recovery requires being patient. ". This is the moment where our sponsors point out that we cannot recover overnight and we should make some efforts and place results of them in God's hands. Many of us have thought "Why I do I feel this way" or "I should be further in this road". Having surrendered our addiction to our Higher Power we began to take inventory and change our lives. This can be done only with practicing spiritual principles of the program on daily basis.
versions.moment: Step by step it gets better - sometimes just for today sometimes just for a minute. We have to face life on its own terms.

versions.quote: 3/16/21 "As recovering addicts, we found that without our drugs we hurt. The program of Narcotics Anonymous provided an opportunity for us to relieve our pain by applying spiritual principles.
versions.body: Every time we used drugs instead of facing life as it is - we suppressed our feelings. It was as if we used drugs to shove them down deep inside where we wouldn't have to deal with it. Some of us started to use to fit in. Some started using to stop pain. For some of us, we used every day. Drugs hurt us so much that we forgot how to live without them. We thought we could handle every problem because we had something to put in our body in one form or another. No matter why we started we all hit a point where we thought drugs were our solution to our problems. Sometimes our disease kept us in a place of fear and isolation. Substances relieved our pain of isolation for a short time and relieved physical pain for a while. Eventually no amount of drugs could relieve our pain. We used more and more trying to make the pain stop yet were tormented as our spirits cried out in agony. The drugs quit working and now they were making the pain worse as they tore us apart from everyone and everything we loved. Eventually we may have found ourselves alone looking at the world at a distance and questioning "why"? When drugs were removed from our bodies the pain intensified as some say "it must get worse before it gets better." We now had to face life. We no longer had a crutch to lean on. Our crutch had been broken. We have to learn how to live without anesthesia, or else we will end up loaded. Every time something in our lives is not turned over to the care of a Higher Power it kicks our asses. Now when we are clean and when we meet the same or similar situations our old feelings long suppressed come to the surface. We are reminded of things from our past. We are able to see our fears for what they are and face them instead of running from them. We are able to change the patterns that ruled our lives for so long. If we continue to hide our feelings we become ashamed of ourselves and need to surrender once again. Narcotics Anonymous helps us learn how to live so that we don't have to suffer anymore. NA is a lifelong solution to our problem of addiction. Without drugs in our systems we have tools we are being taught to use that help with the day to day things that cause us pain. We find that we benefit from daily practice of N.A. suggestions. Calling another addict, calling our Sponsor, attending meetings, writing on the Steps, prayer and reading NA literature written by addicts for addicts. Looking to the spiritual principles gives us the strength to move forward and accomplish another day clean. During this time we develop a 6th sense or intuition of what to say or how to act, but it takes time. Recovery itself takes time. Sometimes, we just need to sit on our hands or do things the opposite of what we did in active addiction. Then and only then, do we discover that somehow God removes our pain - just for today.
versions.moment: We learn how to live Honestly, with Open mindedness and Willingness to try God's way instead of our own. We are given freedom from the insanity drugs gave us with their false hope.

versions.quote: We have learned from our group experience that those who keep coming to our meetings regularly stay clean.
versions.source: What is the Narcotics Anonymous Program pg 15 header par 3 Lines 7-9
versions.body: When we first came to the fellowship of NA we were lost and broken. We came to NA as loners and then found meetings broke our self-built prisons of isolation. For most of us until we surrendered the only thing we did regularly was use drugs. Consistency with anything new was difficult for us. We found a power greater than ourselves in NA meetings. Through meetings we gain strength to stay clean one more day. Other members shared what they learned and passed it to us. Now we know it works. Many of us have found that we cannot stay clean alone. It was suggested to us to go to 90 meetings in 90 days. Regular meeting attendance helps create the footholds for a foundation that we can build on and grow. That foundation is our 12 steps. Our experience is that coming to regular meetings gave us the knowledge of what works for us. We learn what actions we need to take in order to stay clean and recover. We find joy in that we are not alone anymore and don’t feel so isolated. In NA we hear other’s that helps us to see we are not alone. We then are able to open up to others and get vulnerable enough to crack through the thick layers of denial that keep us from seeing our disease exactly as it is. It was only with the Groups experience we learned how to live as we keep coming back one day at a time. As we learn how to communicate with other members we can practice healthy communications outside the Fellowship. We grow by applying spiritual principles both in meetings and society, we get the ability to change ourselves and stay clean while we gain a new sense of freedom.
versions.moment: We stay clean one day at a time, we learn how to share and listen, and we commit ourselves to something bigger than us. NA can be the positive life-school for us.

versions.quote: 10-15-2019 “One of our biggest stumbling blocks seems to be in unrealized expectations of ourselves and others.
versions.body: We come to the fellowship with many hopes and expectations. We come into Narcotics Anonymous and have no real clue who we are. We come to find we have lots of expectations of ourselves and others that we didn’t recognize before. There are few people who are living out their dreams when the found the rooms. We couldn’t accept our imperfections, so we used drugs to hide from our feelings of inadequacy. During our active addiction, to recover seemed an impossible task for us. The literature makes it clear that many of us had to embrace the Gift Of Desperation. When we act on self-will, we have the need to control things that we ought not. This includes the actions of others and their opinions of us. We separated ourselves from the human race with these expectations. We didn’t allow ourselves or others to be humans. When we get caught up in this way of thinking, we lose sight of the program and its effectiveness in our own lives. Once we finally reach the road to recovery. We realize that we were making it harder on ourselves to achieve true happiness. once this happens, we begin to obsess over our own perspectives and fall back into the closed mindedness patterns that brought us here to begin with. When we decide to stop digging, we find our bottom. Once we realize there is another option we are given the opportunities to live the life that we never dreamed that we could live. We always must keep in mind that our real enemy is within us. NA helps us return to the human experience. We gain relationships that never would have been possible before coming to NA. we became humble by getting to know ourselves better. We learned empathy and accepted others for who they are not in spite of who they are.
versions.moment: Too many times we realized we were unprepared to face and embrace our wildest dreams. Recovery provides a lot of blessings in our lives so lets keep our keep head up and our faith strong.

versions.quote: For years, we have avoided seeing ourselves as we really are. We were ashamed of ourselves and felt isolated from the rest of the world.
versions.body:
In active addiction we had no idea of who we were or how others perceived us. The drugs had clouded our minds to the point that we had either forgotten who we were, or we had conjured up in our minds people who we once were or had met. In all situations however we were not who we thought we were. In addiction we were like an invisible person to many, because we were centered in the dope not in life. We were in a prison all by ourselves. A death sentence which was self-imposed. We as Addicts often put ourselves in compromising situations. Being A liar, thief, and schemer became a part of our character and a part of our living Instincts. We needed these instincts to survive our way of living in a drug addicted world. Many of us that went down this path were unable to even look at ourselves in the mirror, let alone take a look inside to see who we really were. We were not someone that we wanted to know. We were a stranger to ourselves.

This in turn led us to a state of isolation. If we are honest with ourselves, we realize this happens because if we didn't want to know ourselves...why would we introduce ourselves to other people. Our only requirement for "friendship" was a matching desire to get loaded and that's as deep as our relationships would go. We felt isolated because of the shame that came along with our actions, attitudes and beliefs. The person we lied to the most is ourselves. Denial was much bigger than we thought when we came into the rooms. It normally takes some time for the fog to wear off before we realize this though.

Many of us didn't want to take an honest look because we were afraid of the ghost in the closet. We kept thinking it may jump out and take the life we had gained, from us.

Until we stopped using, we walked around hollow and dead inside. We didn't have to stay there we found out, as we found addicts that cared in NA. When the fear of change became less than the pain of facing life we chose to recover and try something different. We knew the person that we were before our addiction and knew that we were not that person anymore.
versions.moment: Those who live the Steps find much freedom in writing a thorough and fearless inventory.

versions.quote: Our new found way of life may have its problems. When we ask for help, the road ahead won’t be so rocky.
versions.body: In the past, we thought drugs were the solution and we could solve any problem with them. As addicts we were often stuck in painful patterns that repeated themselves over and over again. Being addicted to our old lifestyle caused us major harm just like all the drugs did. We had to ask, “How do we surrender to the NA way of life?” from someone who has. We have heard it said “If the dope don’t kill us the lifestyle will”. Thinking we were independent was a false idea. Finding out we were interdependent, but refused to ask for help until God humbled us. We found we had no choice until realizing we needed to ask for help from those that had experience. We found it hard to ask for help, but when the pain got great enough we surrendered. In life we find there are rocky roads that may have boulders jump out at us that can cause bumps and bruises. A rough patch of road usually makes us slow down and take the time to gain perspective. We have lived far too long as self-centered individuals, and look at what and where that got us. As human beings, through getting clean, we discover ourselves as whole and complete with the help of others. As we learn to surrender our lives over to the road of recovery we find that in the fellowship of NA we find the help needed to smooth out the road to a new life. We learned to seek a power greater than ourselves instead of continuing down the road of the illusion of control. As we grow, we learn to ask for God's will rather than our own. Without our Higher Power we struggle and toil. The hope that a Higher Power gives us is without parallel, hope is such a gift! It brings new light to our life. We came to NA and met people who found the way to overcome their problems without drugs. We started to learn to ask for help and when we became willing enough to apply solutions, as outlined in the Steps, it made our lives better. The results are in God's hands, now we are not alone against our problems. We learn to not take any shortcuts and buy into the whole program so we don’t short change our process.
versions.moment: Our new perspective gives us the opportunity to see some of the details we may need to look at or revisit to continue on our path of spiritual growth.

versions.quote: We were frightened and ran from the fear, but no matter how far we ran, the fear followed us. We were hopeless, useless and lost.
versions.body:
5-7

When we first arrived in NA we were and had been frightened. Anything new terrified us. Run, run, run that was what some of us did while out using. We ran and kept running. What we eventually figured out was we were running from ourselves. None of us came in on a winning streak. The drugs we used, to run from our fears. It didn't matter how much we used our fears still followed us. Most of us didn't even realize that fear was a way of life for us and no amount of drugs was going to rid us of our fear. It only contributed to further beating us into submission. Some of us acted like we were fearless as we went through our lives. We acted tough to hide from the pain. Some saw great potential but never could finish anything we started. We needed to stop running in order to recover. Our first Step helps turn us around and face our disease. Without knowing we have something to face we can't surrender. We surrender to the fact we have the disease of addiction. If we stop here we will surely die insane. So we seek a power greater than ourselves to restore us to sanity. This is where many surrender to the process of the Steps. At the time we may not understand but we are now becoming willing because of seeing the program working in others' lives. That willingness propels us forward on a great run. Going through the Steps we start doing new things to see If we like them. We are no longer afraid of not being perfect.
versions.moment: We are on a run that isn't running from our disease but instead is running towards a loving, caring God and seeking God's will for our lives.

versions.body: During active addiction, many of us built our walls up not letting anyone in. For years we lived a life focused on self and how we felt things should go. We felt we had no one to turn to or to talk with about our problems. We were untrusting of others and afraid of the vulnerability we felt. We were spiritually void. Completely cut off from the world around us with nothing and no one to turn to. Then, coming into Narcotics Anonymous, we began to grow spiritually, starting from a spark as w heard others talk about their experiences. We saw sharing their pain and hurt. In NA, we learn there is more to life than "just me." We have no program if the "we" of our program is ignored. We become part of something greater than ourselves. We began to let our walls down little by little sharing more in meetings and growing by the process. Spirituality is very important. We learn to let go and let God. By opening up and developing our Spirituality, we save ourselves from the dark void which previously had consumed us. We come to believe in a Higher Power, greater than ourselves, and find spiritual comfort in our lives and to be able to share that spiritual experience with others. Our program is based on spiritual principles and each of us sharing our ESH. We learn our value as individuals in seeking spiritual solutions.
versions.moment: Spirituality and sharing is the essence of our recovery. NA is amazing!

versions.quote: Asking for help in specific terms usually precedes getting that help. By opening the gates of our hearts, we become ready to receive the help we need.
versions.body:
lines 9-10

We came into NA full of ourselves. We may have thought we had all the answers, yet our lives were a mess. Many of us blamed everyone but ourselves for the chaos in our lives. Some knew that their lives were a mess and came in desperate for help. In Step One we ask for help. No matter how we got here all of us had to admit our powerlessness over the disease of addiction and accept that our lives had become unmanageable. Without admitting we needed help we couldn't get help. The 1st Step leaves a void that must be filled. Many of us found this is when we started to truly feel the pain of addiction. We no longer had the drugs to fall back on like a crutch to hold us up. We needed to seek a Power Greater than ourselves to restore us to sanity. The process begins when we get vulnerable and ask for help rather than staying in denial swimming in our excuses.

We build the willingness to ask for help, from a Power greater than ourselves, by witnessing and believing in other addict's restoration to sanity. Open-mindedness is key in turning our belief into faith. When we remain open-minded, we are able to see evidence of a Higher Power at work in the lives of many addicts. This act of witnessing is the personal experience upon which many of us build our faith and willingness to ask for help in learning a new way of life. We learn to not ask for specific things in Step 11 and as we learn how to use the 12 Steps of NA we can grow into that place of manageability with our emotional needs. Today we are learning about how to use the power greater than ourselves in Step Two. As we grow in the program, we begin to realize how important the heart to head connection really is. We now have hope as we see that NA provides us a path to freedom that we hadn't taken before.
versions.moment: This part of the process of surrender opens our minds to try something different. As our books says, it was our way of thinking that got us here. By surrendering to a Power Greater than ourselves, we can now ask for specific things humbly to help our recovery.

versions.quote: 4/13/21 "We are no longer fighting fear, anger, guilt, remorse, self-pity, anxiety, depression and a thousant other ills.
versions.body: We experienced depression all the time. Some of us had suicidal thoughts at a very young age. First, drugs silenced this voice in our heads. After years of using, drugs made this voice stronger. After we quit, we were happy for a while, but then the insanity returned. Our lives surely weren't great when we got to the rooms of Narcotics Anonymous. We had so many issues some said "our issues had issues". We had to get to a point where we truly understood that our way of living was not working and we needed something else. Fear, anger, guilt, self pity, anxiety. depression and a thousand other problems were very familiar to us. Sometimes, giving these up to a power greater than ourselves seemed impossible. We can't avoid our feelings. At times some have found they are not sure if this whole thing works. At least we are clean. Other addicts, said it takes time. They told us we shouldn't leave before the miracle happens. We are learning to surrender. Feelings are just feelings. As long as we allow our crazy thinking to control us, we become more sick. The solution is somewhere in our Higher Power. We just have to learn how to use this source of strength. People say Steps 1,2, and 3 can help with that. We found that there is a Power Greater than ourselves that can restore us to sanity, if we let it. Once we surrender and let go of the control we tried so long to hold onto, things started to change. We began to see that we did not have to live in the insanity that our disease kept us locked up in for so long. We found hope. Sometimes we found hope by seeing others recover and then we thought if they can recover so can "I". The third Step gives us the faith to "let go and let God". We were given a way out of the depravity of our lives. We learn to take responsibility for our actions instead of running from them.
versions.moment: We surrender our will on a moment by moment basis. If we don't, we will suffer and stay in the prison of our own mind.
